references.text: Here Mary Magdalene and Joanna are mentioned among the women who followed Jesus and served him, the same women who are now witnesses at the empty tomb ([ref:Luk 8:2-3|Luke 8:2-3]).
Matthew's account of Mary Magdalene and the other Mary coming to the tomb, parallel to Luke's list of the women at the tomb ([ref:Matt 28:1|Matthew 28:1]).
Mark mentions Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome as the women who came to the tomb with fragrant oils ([ref:Mark 16:1|Mark 16:1]).
John's account of Mary Magdalene coming to the tomb, finding it empty, and then telling the disciples ([ref:Joh 20:1-2|John 20:1-2]).

The travelers on the road to Emmaus refer back to how some women in their group told them about the empty tomb and the vision of angels, confirming the women's testimony in this verse ([ref:Luk 24:22-24|Luke 24:22-24]).

Mark identifies the women who were present at the crucifixion, including Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James, the same ones who later testified to the resurrection ([ref:Mark 15:40-41|Mark 15:40-41]).
The apostles' reaction to the women's testimony: they considered their words idle talk and did not believe them ([ref:Luk 24:11|Luke 24:11]).

The women who had followed Jesus from Galilee saw the tomb and how his body was laid there, and then prepared fragrant oils and spices – this provides the background for their visit to the tomb ([ref:Luk 23:55-56|Luke 23:55-56]).
